summary: Inspected the single new file books/kestrel/jvm/class-file-parser.lisp (189KB, 3872 lines). It is a comprehensive ACL2 formalization of Java class file parsing, containing byte-level parsers, constant pool entry parsers for all 17+ JVM constant types, full class file structure parsing, bytecode instruction translation for 50+ opcodes, attribute parsers (Code, LineNumberTable, LocalVariableTable, etc.), and construction of verified class-info structures. The file includes 100+ defthm statements proving type preservation and well-formedness invariants. This is substantive authored formal mathematics, not a build artifact or certification wrapper.

review_evidence: class-tables.lisp: 1000+ lines defining class-tablep, get-class-info, superclass-okayp, get-superclasses, get-superinterfaces with 50+ defthm statements proving type preservation and well-formedness

floats.lisp: 522 lines formalizing IEEE 754 floating-point with java-floatp/java-doublep recognizers, float<, float=, double<, double=, parsing functions (parse-float, parse-double), and arithmetic operations (fmul) with proofs

jvm-facts.lisp: 813 lines of proof rules for JVM simulation including make-state lemmas, myif lifting, thread-table/heap operations, exception handling, static field map rules, and method lookup properties

jvm.lisp: 343KB, 3000+ lines implementing 50+ bytecode instruction executors (ALOAD, ASTORE, AALOAD, AASTORE, NEWARRAY, TABLESWITCH, RETURN, ARETURN, IRETURN, FRETURN, LRETURN, DRETURN, ARRAYLENGTH, BALOAD, BASTORE, CALOAD, CASTORE, field access, method invocation) with jvm-statep preservation proofs

states.lisp: 725 lines defining JVM state structure (thread-table, heap, class-table, heapref-table, monitor-table, static-field-map, initialized-classes, intern-table) with recognizers, constructors, and invariants
syntax.lisp: 242 lines of syntactic analysis functions for symbolic execution (get-pc-from-state-term, state-size, state-profile) used in proof automation
top.lisp: 77 lines serving as the top-level include book orchestrating 60+ dependency-ordered JVM books
values.lisp: 74 lines defining bit-vector encodings for JVM values (encode-signed, decode-signed, encode-unsigned) with type preservation lemmas
